export default "# Metrics\n\nOpen Metrics from the sidebar to explore time-series metrics without writing ES|QL by hand.\n\n## Namespace overview\n\nPick a namespace from the dropdown to see a wall of sparkline charts — one for every metric in that namespace.\nThe header shows three coverage counts:\n\n- **With data** — metrics that returned at least one non-null value in the selected time range.\n- **No data** — metrics that returned successfully but have no data points in the window.\n- **Failed** — metrics whose queries encountered an error (e.g. timeout, permission denied).\n\nOnly metrics with data are shown as sparkline cards. If any queries failed, expand the **Failed metrics** section below the grid to see each metric name and its failure reason.\n\n### Troubleshooting failed metrics\n\n1. Expand the **Failed metrics** section to review error messages.\n2. Click the search icon next to a failed metric to open its query in **Query Lab** for manual inspection.\n3. Click **Retry failed** to re-run only the failed queries without reloading the entire overview.\n4. If failures persist, check cluster health and permissions in the Console or Cluster Overview page.\n\nClick any chart card to drill into that metric's detail view.\n\n## Metric detail\n\nAfter selecting a metric (from the overview grid or the search bar), you enter detail mode:\n\nChoose an aggregation (including percentiles p50, p95, and p99), then add dimension filters or split by a dimension.\nThe dimension sidebar is scoped to fields relevant to the selected metric's namespace.\n\nUse the time picker and refresh interval in the app header to tune the query window for fast troubleshooting versus long-range trend analysis.\n\nUse View ES|QL to inspect the generated query and validate what the UI is producing. Click the **Explain Query** button in the bottom-right corner of the ES|QL editor to toggle a plain-language explanation of the current query. The explanation is generated by the configured AI provider; if no provider is set up, the panel displays a note to configure one in Settings.\n\nWhen the result looks right, use Edit in Query Lab for manual refinement or Save to Dashboard to create a panel.\n\nUse the **Back to overview** button above the chart to return to the namespace grid.\n\nIf charts are empty, verify the selected namespace and field exist in the chosen time range and remove restrictive dimension filters.\n"
